items.title: AFP defends public arrest of Ben Roberts-Smith
items.description: The Australian Federal Police has detailed intelligence surrounding Ben Roberts-Smith's arrest, pushing back against criticisms of its public nature.

items.title: Young police officer's death raises questions about mental health support
items.description: An inquest into the death of a NSW Police recruit who was less than three months into the job hears differing opinions about whether it was related to his work.

items.title: Live: Hawks in control at Docklands after minute's silence for Daniher
items.description: The Hawks are looking to consolidate a spot in the top four as they take on St Kilda at Docklands, on a day when details of Neale Daniher's state funeral are confirmed. Follow live.

items.title: Australian to join 'scary as hell' mission to rescue Laos villagers from cave
items.description: A diver describes the "emotional moment" when he found a group of men alive after they were trapped for more than a week in a Laos cave, while a South Australian renowned for his ability to navigate tight spaces joins the rescue mission.

items.title: Live: Maroons producing mighty defensive effort to repel rampant Blues
items.description: The Women's State of Origin series wraps up on the Gold Coast, with NSW hunting a clean sweep at a rain-soaked Robina Stadium on the Gold Coast. Follow live.

items.title: Work about to begin on $3.6b Olympic Stadium as protesters vow to stay put
items.description: The Queensland government wants site work to begin on Brisbane's $3.6 billion Olympic stadium on Monday as residents plan a court challenge and Indigenous protesters refuse to move.

items.title: ABC appoints Reuters exec Simon Robinson as news director
items.description: Senior Reuters executive Simon Robinson takes over from former director Justin Stevens who announced his resignation yesterday after four years in the job.

items.title: Nationals pull election stunt as tax debate heats up
items.description: This week a few people got a grilling at Senate estimates, the tax debate heated up and whispers of a new centre-right party fluttered through the press gallery.

items.title: Lawyer says Joshua Brown will admit to childcare centre sex crimes
items.description: Joshua Brown, who has been charged with 156 offences, including sexual assault, has appeared in the Melbourne Magistrates' Court via video link.

items.title: Government sues 3M Australia for $2 billion over PFAS contamination
items.description: The Commonwealth is launching its largest-ever legal claim, suing the manufacturer of a firefighting foam containing PFAS chemicals that contaminated 28 Defence Force bases across Australia.

items.title: U.S. launches new airstrikes in southern Iran amid stalled ceasefire talks

featured_image.name: US forces strike Iranian boats, launch sites in Bandar Abbas

items.description:
The U.S. military carried out new airstrikes in southern Iran targeting a military site believed to pose a threat to American forces and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a U.S. official confirmed on Wednesday. U.S. forces also intercepted and shot down multiple Iranian drones in the region, according to ABC News.[1]

The strikes come as negotiations between Washington and Tehran over a potential peace deal remain unsettled. Speaking at a cabinet meeting Wednesday, President Donald Trump said Iran "wants very much to make a deal" but added, "We're not satisfied with it, but that we will be. Either that or we'll have to just finish the job".[1]

items.title: Israel declares 2,000 sq km of southern Lebanon a combat zone

featured_image.name: Israel launches invasion into southern Lebanon targeting Hezbollah

items.description: Israel's military declared all areas south of the Zahrani River — roughly 2,000 square kilometers of southern Lebanon — a combat zone on Wednesday, warning residents to evacuate northward as it prepares for expanded operations against Hezbollah.[1][2]

items.title: EU sets June 16 date to open Ukraine accession talks

featured_image.name: EU launches formal accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova

items.description: The European Commission is preparing to propose the formal opening of the first cluster of EU membership negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova on June 16, with EU leaders expected to endorse the move at their summit on June 18-19, according to the Kyiv Post. The development comes after nearly two years of deadlock caused by Hungary's veto under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.[1]

items.title: Oil supertankers cross Hormuz as strait traffic inches up

featured_image.name: Why shadow tankers are the only ships still moving through the Strait of  Hormuz

items.description:
Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz showed faint signs of life this week as a COSCO oil products tanker navigated the waterway on Wednesday, a day after two non-Iranian crude supertankers made the crossing — the first time in a week that roughly four million barrels of unsanctioned crude were seen transiting the chokepoint.

The Singapore-linked Eagle Veracruz and Greek-owned Nissos Keros were both observed crossing Hormuz early on Tuesday, carrying crude from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates respectively, according to vessel-tracking data reported by Bloomberg. Overall, five vessels traversed Hormuz in both directions on Tuesday, Bloomberg reported.[1][2]

items.title: White House calls leaked Iran draft deal a 'fabrication'

featured_image.name: Hormuz Flows May Return to Normal Within Month of Deal: Iran TV

items.description: Iranian state television reported on Wednesday that it had obtained a draft of an "initial, unofficial" framework for a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran that would restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to pre-war levels within one month of finalization. The White House quickly pushed back, calling the Iranian report a "total fabrication".[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran state TV says it obtained draft MOU framework with US

featured_image.name: Iran's internet blackout partially lifted after 87 days

items.description: Iran's state television reported on Wednesday that it had obtained a draft of an initial unofficial framework for a Memorandum of Understanding with the United States, according to Reuters. The development marks the latest step in weeks of intensive diplomacy aimed at ending the conflict between Washington and Tehran that began in late February.[1]

items.title: North Korea claims first use of AI in missile tests

featured_image.name: North Korea leader Kim supervised missile test of new guidance system: KCNA

items.description: North Korea on Wednesday announced it had tested a range of advanced weapons systems, including cruise missiles guided by artificial intelligence, marking the first time Pyongyang has publicly claimed to incorporate AI into its missile technology. Leader Kim Jong Un supervised the tests on Tuesday, state media KCNA reported.[1][2][3]

items.title: Cuba calls US oil blockade 'an act of war' at UN Security Council

featured_image.name: US oil, energy blockade 'is an act of war,' Cuba warns at UN

items.description:
Cuba's Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla addressed the United Nations Security Council on Tuesday, warning that the U.S. oil blockade against his country amounts to an act of war and calling on the international community to mobilize against what he described as an unfolding humanitarian catastrophe.

"The oil and energy siege imposed by the United States against Cuba is, in its effects, equivalent to a naval blockade — an act of war," Rodríguez said, according to a statement posted by Cuba's foreign ministry. He added that "the government of the United States, by its deeds, is in a position to erode international peace and security."[1][2]

"I call on the international community to mobilize to prevent a humanitarian catastrophe that could be imposed through arms or the fuel blockade," he told the council, adding that "now should be the time for solidarity with Cuba."[3]

items.title: UK and Poland to sign defense treaty targeting Russian threats

featured_image.name: Britain and Poland are set to sign a big new security treaty

items.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk are set to sign a defence and security treaty in London on Wednesday, marking the latest in a series of bilateral agreements Britain has struck with European partners to confront what officials describe as escalating hostile threats across the continent.

items.title: UN Security Council condemns drone strike on UAE nuclear plant

featured_image.name: Drone strike sparks fire on perimeter of UAE’s Barakah nuclear power plant

items.description: The United Nations Security Council on Tuesday unanimously condemned the drone attack on the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the United Arab Emirates, calling it a violation of international law, according to Reuters. The statement came more than a week after a drone struck an electrical generator at the Arab world's only nuclear power facility on May 17, sparking a fire but causing no injuries or radiation release.[1]

items.title: President Trump Announces U.S. Military Airstrike in Venezuela
items.description: President Trump states the U.S. military conducted its first known airstrike inside Venezuela targeting a dock where drugs were allegedly loaded onto boats[1][2][4].

items.title: Trump Meets Netanyahu at Mar-a-Lago for Gaza Ceasefire Phase Two Talks
items.description: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss advancing phase two of the Gaza ceasefire, including reconstruction and responses to Iran[1][4].

items.title: Feds Launch Massive Taxpayer Fraud Probe in Minnesota After Viral Video
items.description: Federal agencies including DHS, FBI, and ICE investigate $110 million in suspected fraud at Minnesota child care centers following a viral YouTube video[3].

items.title: Americans Express Widespread Opposition to AI Data Centers
items.description: Public backlash against AI infrastructure data centers grows, with protests and demands for bans influencing Democratic Party strategies for future elections[3].

items.title: Elon Musk's Humanoid Robot Vision: China Poised to Lead Production
items.description: China prioritizes humanoid robots in tech race with U.S., ramping up production while warning of industry bubble and potential bottlenecks[3].

items.title: Trump-Putin Call Amid Ukraine-Russia Tensions Over Peace Plan
items.description: President Trump spoke with Putin amid ongoing Ukraine conflict, with Russia reevaluating peace plan tenets after Ukrainian denials[1].

items.title: Democratic Gubernatorial Candidates in Wisconsin Focus on Inflation and Trump
items.description: Seven Democrats vying for Wisconsin governor blame economic issues on Trump and emphasize affordability ahead of 2026 primary[3].
